what_it_does: The edge compute/edge AI layer is the forward-deployed compute substrate and software stack that lets C2, ISR and fires applications run when the enterprise cloud is unreachable. It spans (1) rugged servers and vehicle/dismount-form-factor compute (x86, ARM, NVIDIA Jetson/GPU) hosted in command posts, vehicles, aircraft, ships and on soldiers; (2) container/Kubernetes orchestration and air-gapped software delivery (image registries, package bundles, updates over constrained links); (3) local AI inference (ATR/computer vision, RF classification, LLM assistants) and the lifecycle of those models (packaging, distribution, validation, retraining); (4) data-tier services for DDIL operation: local caching, store-and-forward, conflict-free synchronization when links return, prioritization of what data leaves the node; (5) observability/fleet management for tens to hundreds of nodes without saturating tactical links. In the Army NGC2 architecture this layer is the 'hub' (command-post compute hosting apps locally) and 'spoke' (vehicle nodes) tier of the data mesh; in the Air Force it is the base/ABMS edge node; in the Navy it is shipboard Overmatch compute.

sub_taxonomy.name: S06.1 Rugged edge hardware
sub_taxonomy.note: Vehicle/CP/dismount compute chassis and servers (Klas Voyager now under Anduril, Atmos ATMOS2 selected for NGC2, Crystal Group, Dell rugged/XR, HPE Edgeline, Cubic DTECH, Parsons TECN, Curtiss-Wright/Mercury for airborne, Jetson-based boxes). Largely commoditized at the silicon level; differentiation is SWaP-C, MIL-STD qualification, vehicle integration and program-baseline position.

sub_taxonomy.name: S06.2 Air-gapped delivery and edge orchestration
sub_taxonomy.note: Kubernetes distributions and disconnected delivery: Defense Unicorns UDS/Zarf, Platform One Big Bang/Iron Bank, Rancher Government (RKE2/K3s), Red Hat MicroShift/Device Edge, Spectro Cloud Palette Edge, SUSE/ZEDEDA. The most mature commercial-to-DoD sub-segment; one unicorn already exists.

sub_taxonomy.name: S06.3 Edge AI inference and model lifecycle
sub_taxonomy.note: On-device/on-node ATR, CV, RF and LLM inference plus model packaging, distribution, validation and retraining at the edge: TurbineOne Frontline, Striveworks Chariot, EdgeRunner AI, Ozni AI (SBIR), Palantir (edge Foundry/AIP), Anduril Lattice, Army Project Linchpin (MLOps pipeline). Less mature; first large FFP award (TurbineOne, $98.9M, Sep 2025) signals transition.

sub_taxonomy.name: S06.4 DDIL data synchronization and prioritization
sub_taxonomy.note: Local-first data, CRDT/peer-to-peer sync (Ditto), pub-sub in DIL (WPL VERBENA SBIR), hub-and-spoke reconciliation as demonstrated in Ivy Mass. Partially solved inside the NGC2 data mesh primes; standalone commercial products exist but evidence of scaled military deployment is thin.

sub_taxonomy.name: S06.5 Edge observability and fleet operations
sub_taxonomy.note: Health, version, and security state of many nodes (65+ in Ivy Sting 5) without radiating or saturating links; day-2 operations by soldiers rather than DevOps engineers. Least evidenced sub-segment; mostly INFERENCE that this is a pain.

sub_taxonomy.name: S06.6 Integration/accreditation of apps onto edge platforms
sub_taxonomy.note: Getting third-party apps onto accredited edge platforms (cATO, Iron Bank hardening, Game Warden). Overlaps S06.2; commercial vendors include Second Front, Defense Unicorns, Anchore, RegScale.

current_architecture.description: Army NGC2 (the most visible 2025-2026 architecture) is a hub-and-spoke edge data mesh: command-post hubs host compute and local applications for DDIL operation, vehicle spokes access those applications on the move, and a division cloud provides the upper tier. current_architecture.security_domain: Predominantly SECRET (S//REL) at brigade and above for C2 data, with unclassified/CUI enclaves for sensors and sustainment; cross-domain solutions required to bridge; Army RFI on CDS hardware/software architecture for mission command exists (orangeslices.ai). Edge nodes must host mixed IL levels and support classified networks that cannot phone home.
current_architecture.connectivity_dependency: Designed to be cloud-optional: NGC2 hubs continue serving apps without the division cloud; spokes depend on hub reachability for shared services. Software delivery, model updates, telemetry and licensing all traditionally assume connectivity and are the parts most likely to break.
current_architecture.what_breaks_when_disconnected: Demonstrated to survive in Ivy Mass: local battle tracking with later synchronization. Still fragile (INFERENCE from architecture and vendor claims): image pulls/updates without local registries, license and identity checks that assume enterprise reachability, model updates and retraining feedback loops, fleet observability, conflict resolution for concurrently edited COP objects, and the operator burden of reconciling versions across many nodes after partition.

technical_difficulty.summary: Hardware is commoditized (Jetson/x86 in MIL-STD chassis from a dozen vendors). Orchestration for air-gapped delivery is largely solved by open-source Zarf/UDS plus Big Bang, with the residual difficulty being fleet-scale day-2 operations by non-experts. The genuinely hard, under-solved problems are (a) model lifecycle at the edge under DDIL (safe, bandwidth-aware distribution; validation against sensor/environment drift; soldier-driven retraining with provenance), (b) principled data prioritization and conflict resolution across partitions at scale (65+ nodes), and (c) doing all of this inside classification, accreditation and EMCON constraints that commercial edge tooling ignores (no telemetry home, no license phone-home, multi-level enclaves, cross-domain).
required_expertise: Kubernetes internals and air-gapped delivery (Zarf/UDS, Big Bang, RKE2/K3s)
Distributed systems: partition tolerance, CRDTs, gossip/pub-sub under intermittent links
Edge ML deployment (TensorRT/ONNX on Jetson, quantization, on-device training) and MLOps
Tactical networking (bandwidth budgets, EMCON, mesh radios, PACE plans)
DoD security architecture (cATO, Iron Bank hardening, IL levels, CDS interfaces, STIGs)
Hardware sympathy: thermal/power envelopes of vehicle-mounted compute
technical_difficulty.hardest_problem: Keeping tens to hundreds of heterogeneous edge nodes at a known-good software and model state, and reconciling their data, when links are intermittent, bandwidth is contested, radiating is dangerous and the operators are soldiers rather than SREs - while every artifact remains accreditable.
technical_difficulty.commodity_parts: Rugged chassis and servers; NVIDIA Jetson/GPU modules; Kubernetes distributions; container registries; basic OTA update mechanisms; standard CV models; commercial fleet-management dashboards.

capital_intensity.assumptions: PoC: two founders, consumer/Jetson devkits, open-source K8s and public CV datasets, simulated DDIL links. Credible demo: 3-6 engineers for 9-18 months, 2-4 rugged nodes ($15k-$60k each), MIL-STD/EMI pre-testing, exercise participation costs (travel, a lab), an IL4/IL5 dev environment, SBIR Phase I/II or DIU CSO funding covering most of it. First production: cATO/Iron Bank hardening, integration onto NGC2/Overmatch baselines through a prime, 24/7 support, FSO and possibly a cleared facility, 12-24 months of sales cycle burn. Ranges are HYPOTHESIS grounded in comparable startup trajectories (TurbineOne raised $36M before a $98.9M FFP; Defense Unicorns raised $15M STRATFI before scaling).

regulatory_access.prototype_with_commercial_unclassified_d: yes - orchestration, sync and model-lifecycle tooling can be built and demonstrated on open-source stacks and public datasets; realism comes from partnering with a unit or SBIR sponsor for CUI data later.
regulatory_access.government_data_required: Not for the platform layer; required for ATR model quality (sensor-specific imagery) and for proving value on real mission threads. CUI and later SECRET data become necessary at the integration stage.
regulatory_access.itar_ear: Generic edge software and COTS compute are typically EAR (EAR99 or 5D002 for crypto). Software 'specially designed' for military ATR, fire control or C2 integration can fall under ITAR USML Category XI(d)/XXI or be treated as defense articles by primes; hardware in military chassis may be Category XI. Requires export-control counsel; deemed-export rules affect the non-US-person founder.
regulatory_access.cui_likely: Yes - any work touching NGC2 data models, unit SOPs, exercise results or program documentation will be CUI; requires NIST SP 800-171/CMMC posture.
regulatory_access.classified_integration_eventually: Yes - brigade-and-above C2 runs on SECRET networks; production integration will require cleared personnel and a facility or a prime/host partner with one.
regulatory_access.cleared_personnel_at_mvp: No for MVP; yes by first production deployment (INFERENCE from NGC2 security domain).
regulatory_access.non_us_person_founder_note: The Indonesian founder (not assumed a US person) creates deemed-export exposure for any ITAR/EAR-controlled technical data, potential FOCI concerns if they hold significant equity/control, and ineligibility for personnel clearances. SBIR/STTR requires the small business to be more than 50% owned and controlled by US citizens or permanent residents (the German founder qualifies once an LPR). DIU CSOs and OTAs have no citizenship requirement per se but ITAR authorization is still needed to share controlled data. Mitigations to review with counsel: keep the non-US founder on the EAR99/open-source platform side, structured equity, technology control plan, or a US-person-controlled entity. Not a legal judgment - specialist review required.

why_not_solved.explanation: For the hardware substrate and air-gapped delivery mechanics, the problem is substantially solved: commodity rugged compute from many vendors, Zarf/UDS/Big Bang for delivery, and NGC2 hubs demonstrated local operation with later sync. Startups entering here compete against an incumbent unicorn and a vertically integrated prime (Anduril+Klas).

On-device training/inference on Jetson-class hardware, CRDT sync libraries and LLM-based sense-making at the edge became practical only since ~2022-2024, which is why model lifecycle and DIL data services are still SBIR/first-award stage.

NGC2 data mesh internals (Lattice, Foundry, Raft) are vendor-controlled; third-party edge services must integrate through the prime's APIs and registries, which limits standalone products and pushes startups into subcontract roles.

Every container, model and node must be accreditable (cATO, Iron Bank, STIGs, CDS). Commercial edge tools that phone home for licensing, telemetry or registries fail these constraints, and re-engineering them for EMCON/air-gap is slow.

Heterogeneous radios, vehicles, enclaves and legacy programs of record (per GAO, services in isolation) mean every deployment is a bespoke integration; this is why Picogrid earns a stream of small integration contracts rather than one large product buy.
PEO C3N, PEO IEW&S, AFLCMC, NAVWAR, MCSC, CDAO and DIU each buy edge capability separately; there is no single edge compute program office, so scaling requires multiple parallel captures.

Rugged hardware margins are thin and volumes small; software value accrues to whoever owns the data layer. Point solutions (sync, observability) are features from the prime's perspective and are hard to sell standalone.

attractiveness.bull: Real money is now moving: $99.6M NGC2 prototype, June 2026 baseline award, $98.9M FFP for edge ATR, $136M Series B for air-gapped delivery, repeated Phase III awards. The Army has an explicit organization (PM C2 Infrastructure) for edge compute and a serialized exercise cadence (Ivy Sting, Ivy Mass, PC-C6) that gives startups concrete integration events. Model lifecycle and DIL data prioritization are recognized but immature - a small, technically strong team can build a credible open-source-based wedge on unclassified data and enter via SBIR Phase I/II, DIU CSO or a prime's NGC2 team.
attractiveness.bear: Hardware is commoditized and consolidating (Anduril bought Klas; Atmos is the NGC2 hardware baseline). Delivery/orchestration is owned by a $1B incumbent with a GSA vehicle. Data mesh and model tooling inside NGC2 are controlled by Anduril/Palantir/Raft/Striveworks, and the June 2026 baseline award makes that team the gatekeeper. Remaining gaps look like features, not companies. Classification and accreditation force cleared staff early, and the non-US-person founder complicates ITAR and SBIR ownership rules. Absence of a visible standalone competitor in observability/sync is not evidence of demand.
attractiveness.verdict: Medium-low for a $250k two-founder team as a standalone edge platform; medium as a narrow, prime-integrated software wedge (edge model validation/distribution or bandwidth-aware data prioritization) pursued via SBIR/DIU with a subcontract path onto NGC2 or Overmatch.

market_stage.rationale: Within five years the sequence has moved from RFIs and pilots (2022-2024) through prototype OTAs (2025) to the first post-prototype baseline award and FFP fielding contracts (2025-2026). Repeat/production is not yet demonstrated at scale (PC-C6 pending; obligations undisclosed), so the segment is Transitioning rather than Mature.

proto_purgatory.notes: Purgatory is visible but escapable. Picogrid shows the pattern of many small unit-level awards ($1.1M Army, XVIII ABN, SIGINT, c-UAS) before a $9.3M Phase III - still not a program of record. SBIR-stage DIL data projects (WPL, Ozni, Tiami) show repeated SBIR funding without evident transition. Counter-examples: Defense Unicorns escaped via STRATFI plus a GSA vehicle and four-service Phase IIIs; TurbineOne escaped via a $98.9M FFP; NGC2 moved from prototype OTA to a baseline award within 11 months.
proto_purgatory.opportunity_or_warning: Mixed: opportunity for software that lands on an accredited baseline (NGC2, Big Bang) via a prime or Phase III, warning for standalone edge point solutions and for hardware. The escape path runs through primes and SBIR Phase III, which for a two-founder team means an early subcontract/partner strategy rather than direct program capture.

candidate_gaps.title: Edge model lifecycle under DDIL: validate, distribute and roll back ATR/CV models across many nodes over contested links
candidate_gaps.problem_one_sentence: Once ATR/CV models are trained or updated at the edge, there is no evidenced, accredited way to validate them against the local sensor/environment, distribute deltas over constrained links to 65+ nodes, track which model version is running where, and roll back safely.
candidate_gaps.user: Brigade/division S2 sections and unit tech teams running Frontline-class ATR and NGC2 decision tools; PEO IEW&S/PM C2 Infrastructure as program owners.
candidate_gaps.current_workflow: 1) Model trained centrally (Linchpin-style pipeline) or on-device by soldiers; 2) packaged as container/ONNX; 3) pushed via Zarf/UDS bundle or vendor-specific data mesh when a link exists; 4) node operators manually confirm version; 5) performance drift discovered anecdotally during exercises; 6) retraining loop closed by sending data back when bandwidth allows.
candidate_gaps.current_solution: Vendor-integrated: TurbineOne (on-device training), Striveworks Chariot (MLOps) inside Team Anduril, Palantir AIP, Anduril Lattice model deployment; generic: Zarf bundles.
candidate_gaps.failure_point: No independent validation gate for models arriving at a node; full-model pushes exceed bandwidth budgets; version state across nodes is opaque after partitions; rollback is manual; provenance/T&E evidence for accreditation is ad hoc (INFERENCE from architecture and public statements; no primary document describes the failure explicitly).

evidence.claim: Army paid $98.9M FFP for on-device ATR where all data is processed on soldiers' devices, signalling that cloud-dependent model pipelines are unacceptable at the edge
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: Team Anduril scaled to 65+ edge nodes and 20+ applications at Ivy Sting 5, creating the fleet-scale version-management problem
evidence.label: FACT (company-reported)

evidence.claim: ATEC is transforming test and evaluation for NGC2, implying that evaluating continuously updated software/models is an open institutional problem
evidence.label: INFERENCE

evidence.claim: SBIR-stage projects (Ozni AI NEMESIS LLM-on-sensor) show edge inference lifecycle still at prototype maturity
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: DoW AI Strategy Pace-Setting Projects require demonstrations by July 2026, creating budget pull for AI-enabled battle management at the edge
evidence.label: FACT (secondary)

candidate_gaps.why_startups_havent_solved: Model tooling is being absorbed into the NGC2 primes' stacks (Striveworks/Palantir/Anduril); standalone MLOps vendors lack edge/DDIL and accreditation focus; the problem became real only when node counts and on-device training scaled in 2025-2026.
candidate_gaps.incumbent_response_risk: High - Striveworks and Palantir can add validation/distribution features; Anduril controls the data layer APIs.
candidate_gaps.technical_wedge_hypothesis: A bandwidth-aware model distribution and validation service: delta/patch model updates with per-node validation against a held-out local sensor sample, signed provenance manifests usable as accreditation evidence, and a partition-tolerant version ledger; delivered as a Zarf-packaged component that runs beside any inference runtime.
candidate_gaps.mvp_sketch: Open-source-based prototype on 3-5 Jetson nodes with simulated DDIL links (tc/netem): delta model updates, local validation harness on public datasets (e.g., xView/DOTA), CRDT version ledger, dashboard that works over kilobit links; demo rollback after a bad model.
candidate_gaps.data_requirement: Public overhead/EO datasets for MVP; CUI sensor imagery from a sponsor unit for credibility; eventually SECRET for program integration.
candidate_gaps.integration_requirement: Must integrate with Zarf/UDS or Big Bang packaging and expose APIs to Lattice/Foundry/Chariot; hardware-agnostic (Jetson, x86 GPU).
candidate_gaps.entry_vehicle: Army/AF SBIR Phase I-II (edge AI topics), DIU CSO, or subcontract to a Team Anduril/Lockheed member for PC-C6; xTech-style competitions.
candidate_gaps.why_now: Node counts and on-device training are scaling (65+ nodes), NGC2 baseline award (Jun 2026) fixes the platform to integrate against, and July 2026 Pace-Setting demonstrations create demand for evidence of model trustworthiness.
candidate_gaps.killer_risk: The primes treat this as a feature and close it within 12 months; without a data-layer position the startup is a subcontractor with no pricing power.

candidate_gaps.title: Bandwidth-aware data prioritization and reconciliation across partitioned edge nodes
candidate_gaps.problem_one_sentence: When links are intermittent, nodes need a policy-driven way to decide what data leaves first, at what fidelity, and how conflicting COP edits are reconciled on reconnection - today this is handled by vendor-specific mesh logic and manual deconfliction.
candidate_gaps.user: Division/brigade G6/S6, hub operators, fires and intel cells whose products compete for the same links.
candidate_gaps.current_workflow: 1) Hub loses division cloud; 2) apps keep local state; 3) on reconnection the data mesh replicates whatever it can; 4) operators deconflict duplicate/conflicting track and graphic objects by hand; 5) large products (FMV, imagery) are pushed opportunistically or not at all.
candidate_gaps.current_solution: Anduril/Palantir data mesh replication inside NGC2; Ditto CRDT sync in pilots; SBIR-stage pub-sub (WPL VERBENA).
candidate_gaps.failure_point: Prioritization is not policy-driven by mission phase; replication logic is opaque to operators; conflict resolution semantics for C2 objects are vendor-specific (INFERENCE).

candidate_gaps.why_startups_havent_solved: Sync is embedded inside the data mesh primes; a standalone sync layer has to be adopted by the prime, and Ditto already occupies the commercial niche without evidenced scaled military deployment.
candidate_gaps.incumbent_response_risk: High - this is core data-layer functionality for Anduril/Palantir.
candidate_gaps.technical_wedge_hypothesis: Mission-phase-aware prioritization and fidelity-degradation engine (e.g., send track updates before imagery; downsample FMV) with explicit, auditable conflict-resolution rules for C2 object types, exposed as a sidecar the mesh can call.
candidate_gaps.mvp_sketch: Simulated brigade with 10 nodes and netem-shaped links; open CoT/TAK data; demonstrate mission-critical latency reduction and zero duplicate tracks after 30-minute partitions versus naive replication.
candidate_gaps.data_requirement: Synthetic/TAK data for MVP; exercise data (CUI) to tune.
candidate_gaps.integration_requirement: TAK/CoT and NGC2 data layer APIs; must run inside the prime's Kubernetes environment.
candidate_gaps.entry_vehicle: SBIR (Army C5ISR Center / AFRL topics on DIL data), or partner with Raft/Ditto.
candidate_gaps.why_now: Division-scale NGC2 exercises now create measurable partition events; PC-C6 is a demonstration venue.
candidate_gaps.killer_risk: Feature, not product: incumbents implement it; no independent buyer.

candidate_gaps.title: Low-signature edge fleet observability and day-2 operations for soldier-operated nodes
candidate_gaps.problem_one_sentence: Tens to hundreds of edge nodes need health, version, security and capacity visibility without radiating or consuming scarce bandwidth, and remediation that a signal soldier (not an SRE) can execute.
candidate_gaps.user: G6/S6 sections, PM C2 Infrastructure field support, unit tech teams.
candidate_gaps.current_workflow: 1) Nodes provisioned by vendor FSRs/contractor field support; 2) status checked by walking to the node or via vendor dashboards that assume connectivity; 3) issues escalated to contractor support; 4) version drift discovered during exercises.
candidate_gaps.current_solution: Vendor dashboards (Lattice, UDS), Big Bang monitoring stack (Prometheus/Grafana) designed for connected clusters; contractor field support.
candidate_gaps.failure_point: Observability stacks are chatty and assume uplink; no EMCON-aware telemetry budgeting; soldier-executable runbooks are limited (HYPOTHESIS - no primary document found this session).

candidate_gaps.why_startups_havent_solved: Commercial observability vendors have no DDIL/EMCON model; defense primes bundle basic dashboards; the buyer historically outsourced day-2 ops to contractor field support rather than buying tooling.

candidate_gaps.technical_wedge_hypothesis: Telemetry-budgeted, store-and-forward observability agent with EMCON modes and soldier-facing remediation runbooks, packaged as a UDS/Zarf component.
